the NF2 gene is inactivated by point mutation in the majority of meningiomas.
we have identified in 24 of 151 sporadic meningioma samples 24 mutations in the neurofibromatostosis 2 gene (a tumour suppressor).
the neurofibromatostis type 2 (NF2) gene is inactivated by mutations in sporadic meningioma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of genetic alterations in meningiomas.
the molecular genetics of meningiomas and their possible relationship with neurofibromatose type 2 (NF2) gene.
the identification of the genetic alterations that occur during the development and progression of human brain tumours and their application in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF2 gene is the most likely candidate for the meningioma gene on chromosome 2q.
the NF2 gene is inactivated by a variety of mechanisms in 60% and another gene in the other 40% of sporadic tumours.
the NF2 gene is involved in 60% and a second as yet unknown gene in the remaining 40% of sporadic tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NF2 gene was found to be mutated in all of the meningiomas that lost heterozygosity at 22q.
NF2 is inactivated in 60% and another gene in 40% of sporadic tumours.
the NF2 gene is involved in 100% of sporadic and 50% of familial meningiomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NF2 is a tumour suppresser gene, which is involved in 60% meningiomas.
the NF2 gene is the major gene involved in sporadic meningioma, and that the other 40% of sporadic cases are caused by other mechanisms.
the vast majority of sporadic (non-inherited) meningiomas have a genetic alteration that inactivates the NF2 gene.
